newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Gov't tries to consolidate CVRD cases in one court.
newsitem.headline: Gov't tries to consolidate CVRD cases in one court.

text.p: A Brazilian judge was studying Wednesday a latest attempt by the government to undo injunctions blocking the privatization of Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), a court spokesman said.

The judge, Justice Democrito Ramos Reinaldo of the Superior Justice Tribunal (STJ), was working on a case brought by the government to consolidate injunctions that have been filed across the country under one court, making it easier to address them.
The judge might announce his verdict later Wednesday, the spokesman said.
The STJ is the highest federal court in Brazil for cases not involving constitutional matters, which are judged at the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF).

Government lawyers lodged a so-called Conflict of Interpretation action with the STJ Tuesday in an attempt to send all outstanding and future injunctions against the CVRD sale to a single court in Brasilia.
The move would simplify the government's attempts to overturn the injunctions, which have been issued by courts across Brazil.

But the spokesman could not confirm speculation that a verdict in favor of the government would automatically crush an injunction against the sale issued last week by a Sao Paulo judge and which the government has failed to overturn.
"There's a lot of debate raging precisely about that question. I think we'll have to wait and see what the judge says," the spokesman said.

Last week, the National Development Bank (BNDES) lodged a similar case with the STJ which was also received by Justice Reinaldo. The bank then withdrew the action after the judge issued a preliminary opinion against the case.
The STJ spokesman said he believed the government's new Conflict of Interpretation case had been drawn up with more attention to detail.

Faced with the injunctions, the BNDES was forced to postpone Tuesday's scheduled privatization auction of a 45 percent block of CVRD voting shares. Bank officials have said they will hold the auction once the injunctions are defeated.
